subject: Re: ApolloGen - segmented retention confirmation & SOC 2 evidence
messages:
From: ApolloGen Audit Team <audit@apollogen.com>
To: marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 30 Jul 2028 21:22:00 -0700
Subject: Request: tenant-scoped log retention evidence + SOC 2 mapping

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for taking our quick SOC 2 follow-up. As we evaluate Redwood for a procurement decision, the audit team has two specific asks regarding tenant-scoped telemetry and deletion mechanics:

1) Can you provide evidence that short-lived session traces (debug snapshots, ephemeral KV cache entries) are deleted within the customer-level TTL (we have a 30-day requirement for our PII-linked traces)? We need both the policy excerpt and an example proof-of-delete artifact.
2) ApolloGen runs a hybrid deployment (hosted + private VPC). We need confirmation of any exceptions for private deployments where retention may differ and the procedure to request a customer-specific retention variance.

If possible, please include a simple matrix that maps Redwood log buckets (session-trace, access-log, audit-trail, kvcache) to retention windows and the artifact types you can deliver (log export, delete certificate, sampling proof).

Ideally we get this by Wednesday so our security reviewer can close the SOC 2 checklist.

Best,
Elle Moreau
Senior Auditor
ApolloGen

[Attachment: apollogen-questionnaire-soc2.xlsx]

From: marissa.co.le@redwood.ai <marissa.co.le@redwood.ai>
To: ApolloGen Audit Team <audit@apollogen.com>
Cc: procurement@apollogen.com
Date: Tue, 31 Jul 2028 09:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: tenant-scoped log retention evidence + SOC 2 mapping

Elle —

Thanks for the clear list. We can provide the policy excerpts and a small evidence bundle. Quick summary up front so your reviewer can triage:

- Short-lived session traces (what we label "session-trace"/"ephemeral-debug") default to 30 days in our hosted environment; we can provide a sample proof-of-delete (export showing deleted object ids + deletion timestamp) and a redacted sample of the backing audit record.
- KV cache entries (transient model keys) are retained for up to 7 days by default; however, for dedicated/private deployments customers can opt into a longer local TTL — that requires a signed retention variance request and is subject to controls review.
- Audit trails and immutable access logs default to 365 days for hosted and to customer-configurable windows for Private deployments (we include per-tenant export endpoints for on-prem retention).

We're attaching a short mapping matrix and two sample artifacts (proof-of-delete PDF + CSV index of SOC 2 artifacts). There are a couple of items we may need to coordinate with you: any specific claimant identifiers you need included in the proof-of-delete (customer tenant id vs. external user id) and whether you want a notarized or internally-signed deletion certificate.

I'll also loop in Kimberly from Security for the variance workflow and the technical steps for Private deployments.

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Sr. Customer Trust Manager
Redwood Inference

[Attachments: apollogen-retention-matrix.xlsx, proof-of-delete-sample.pdf, soc2-artifact-index.csv]

From: marissa.co.le@redwood.ai <marissa.co.le@redwood.ai>
To: kimberly.park@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 31 Jul 2028 09:19:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: ApolloGen - retention evidence request (need variance path)

Kimberly —

Forwarding ApolloGen's ask. Two things I'd like your guidance on:

1) For ApolloGen's Private VPC nodes, they want to know the exact process and controls for approving a longer retention on session traces (they expect some legal/regulatory justification). What's our recommended minimum control set to allow an exception (e.g., E2 encryption at rest + local RBAC + audit snapshot retention)?

2) For the proof-of-delete artifact, I'm preparing a redacted sample. Is the CSV index enough for SOC 2 or should we provide a signed deletion certificate (we have a templated one but I've seen requests for third-party notarization).

Proposed reply (short): Confirm default windows, attach matrix & artifacts, outline variance process (formal request -> security review -> documented approval -> artifact delivery). If you can draft the variance checklist items, I'll include them.

Thanks,
Marissa

From: kimberly.park@redwood.ai <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: marissa.co.le@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 31 Jul 2028 10:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: ApolloGen - retention evidence request (need variance path)

Marissa —

Thanks for the ping. Proposed variance control baseline:

- Written business justification with tenant-scoped legal/regulatory citation;
- Configured encryption keys (KMS) with customer-managed key option for Private deployments;
- RBAC proof (who can request exports/deletes) + 2-person approval for variance activation;
- Timeboxed variance window with automatic re-review at expiration;
- Signed deletion certificate generation on completion (internally-signed template is acceptable for SOC 2; notarization is not required unless the customer mandates it).

About artifacts: provide both the CSV index (contains object ids, deletion timestamps, and correlating audit log entry ids) plus a short PDF certificate signed by our Trust team. That combination is what usually satisfies SOC 2 reviewers.

I'll attach a checklist snippet you can copy into the reply.

Kimberly Park
Director, Security Assurance
Redwood Inference

[Attachment: variance-checklist-snippet.md]

From: marissa.co.le@redwood.ai <marissa.co.le@redwood.ai>
To: ApolloGen Audit Team <audit@apollogen.com>
Cc: procurement@apollogen.com, kimberly.park@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 01 Aug 2028 10:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: tenant-scoped log retention evidence + SOC 2 mapping — evidence bundle attached

Elle —

Attached is a concise evidence bundle for your SOC 2 reviewer and procurement team:

- apollogen-retention-matrix.xlsx — maps our internal buckets to default retention windows and artifact types (column: bucket / default-ttl / private-ttl-option / artifact-available).
- proof-of-delete-sample.pdf — redacted sample containing tenant id, object ids, deletion timestamp, and redwood Trust signature.
- soc2-artifact-index.csv — index of artifacts we can provide for each bucket (with example file names and GUIDs).

Summary answers to your specific questions:

1) Short-lived session traces in Hosted: default 30 days. We can deliver a CSV of deleted object ids + an internally-signed deletion certificate. For Private (VPC) nodes, customers may request a variance; approval requires the variance checklist below.

2) Variance workflow (high level):
   a) Customer submits a Retention Variance Request (tenant id, business/legal rationale, desired TTL).
   b) Security + Product review controls & risks.
   c) If approved, variance is timeboxed and recorded on the tenant's compliance docket; artifacts produced at variance end.

Variance checklist (high level): business justification, KMS configuration, RBAC attestation, two-person approval for variance activation, and scheduled re-review. Kimberly attached a checklist snippet.

Please confirm if the CSV index and the internally-signed certificate meet your SOC 2 reviewer needs or if you'd like the certificate notarized (we can do that but it adds lead time). If you need tenant-specific proof with payload-level ids rather than redacted ids, let us know and we'll scope a sanitized export.

I'll stand by for any follow-ups — happy to jump on a short call with your auditor if helpful.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Sr. Customer Trust Manager
Redwood Inference

[Attachments: apollogen-retention-matrix.xlsx, proof-of-delete-sample.pdf, soc2-artifact-index.csv]
